determinism.observed: Both builds produced the identical member hash 4136587a and zip digest 4sDK8P5m. The after-planes agree. The five statuses are 200, 403, 403, 200, 403 and the rollback decision was computed from the three after-integers alone -- which is this order's own mechanism, written in response to my round-7 near miss where a multi-line shell capture compared against a string announced a rollback the data inside the same alarm contradicted. This time the helper prints the human block to stderr and EXACTLY the integer to stdout, so a caller that captures stdout gets an integer and nothing else. ONE ERROR OF MINE IN THIS ORDER, caught and corrected before it was reported: the first log window was 30 minutes wide and so counted S2's pre-apply refusal as if it were this release's, giving 2 where 1 was expected. Rescoping to the apply's own LastModified gives 1 and 1.
